observations: Photo 0 shows two large gas cylinders side by side, one greyish-green and one reddish-brown, with a digital weighing scale between them.
The greyish-green cylinder on the left has a metal collar at the top with a valve and a small white tag; it appears worn and slightly corroded.
The reddish-brown cylinder on the right has a black hose attached to its valve and shows significant rust and paint peeling.
Photo 1 is similar to photo 0 but with the black hose now connected to the left cylinder, suggesting it is being tested or used.
Photo 2 is nearly identical to photo 0, with the hose disconnected from the left cylinder and resting on the right one.
All three photos show the same setup: two cylinders, a scale, and a corrugated metal wall background.
No visible brand or model markings are readable on either cylinder.
The scale is digital but its display is not legible in any photo.
The seller claims '50 kg gas cylinder', 'util valve', 'no issue', 'no leakages'.

claims.evidence: The scale is present but its display is not legible in any photo; no markings on the cylinders indicate capacity.
The valve on the left cylinder is visible but no text or markings identify it as a 'util valve'; the term is not standard and may be seller-specific.
No internal inspection or pressure test is visible; condition beyond surface rust cannot be assessed remotely.
No leak test (e.g., soapy water) is shown; the presence of a hose does not prove no leakage.
